newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Pedestrians and cars are a deadly mix in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Pedestrians and cars are a deadly mix in Bogota.

text.p: Traffic accidents are the second leading cause of violent death in Bogota and most involve pedestrians run down while trying to cross the city's chaotic streets, Colombia's leading daily said on Friday.

El Tiempo, citing figures from the Forensic Medical Institute, said a record total of 840 pedestrians were run down and killed in the city of about six million people between January 1995 and June 1996.

Drunk drivers are part of the problem but so too are drunk pedestrians, the newspaper said. Of the 472 pedestrians killed in 1995, it said blood tests were performed on 370. In 200 cases, the tests came back showing blood-alcohol levels high enough to indicate the pedestrians were "walking under the influence" when killed.

Only 51 drivers and 72 passengers were killed in traffic accidents in Bogota during the same 18-month period in which 840 pedestrians were killed, according to El Tiempo. It noted that guns were still the leading cause of violent death in Bogota, which has one of the highest murder rates in the world.
